name: python-tooling
check: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' && ruff check .

not_planted.K7: K7 is reserved for python-service, where an external boundary is worth stubbing.
not_planted.K9: K9 does not apply to this stdlib-only dialect because it has no dependency manifest or lock.

declared.text: User-supplied helper names are passed as argument-vector entries, never interpolated into a shell command.

faults.finding: The helper name is interpolated into an os.system shell line despite the argv declaration.

neighbour.why_clean: The neighbouring helper passes the same value as one entry in a subprocess argument list.

declared.text: Record paths always remain beneath the configured store root.

faults.finding: The record path joins an untrusted name without resolving and checking containment under the root.

neighbour.why_clean: The checked neighbour proves the resolved candidate is relative to the resolved root.

declared.text: A count of zero is an answer and is distinct from an absent record.

faults.finding: The count renderer uses truthiness and therefore reports a stored zero as absent.

neighbour.why_clean: The optional-label neighbour distinguishes absence explicitly with is None.

declared.text: Credentials never leave the process in failure logs.

faults.finding: The failure logger serializes the entire process environment, including credentials.

neighbour.why_clean: The neighbouring failure log emits a fixed redaction marker instead of the token.

declared.text: An unreadable or corrupt store is reported as a refusal, never served as an empty answer.

faults.finding: The store catches every read or decode failure and returns an empty list that looks authoritative.

neighbour.why_clean: The read boundary catches only I/O failure and immediately re-raises it.

declared.text: Intervals are half-open, including their start and excluding their end.

faults.finding: Interval.contains uses an inclusive end although the model declares a half-open interval.

neighbour.why_clean: The values neighbour uses Python's half-open range with the same start and end.

declared.text: Test oracles are independent literals, not values computed by the code under test.

faults.finding: The fixture-case test calculates its expected checksum by calling the checksum function itself.

neighbour.why_clean: The neighbouring checksum test supplies a literal expected value independent of the function.
